sentence: Gels are crosslinked networks of polymer chains swollen by solvent. Above the gelation threshold the network bears stress and shows a non-zero elastic modulus, while below it the system flows as a viscous liquid. Critical gel theory predicts a power-law stress relaxation modulus G(t) proportional to t^{-n} with n near 2/3 at the gel point, capturing the diverging longest relaxation time and the scale-free network structure at criticality.

Liquid-gas critical points exhibit the same universality class as the three-dimensional Ising model, with the gas-liquid density difference playing the role of order parameter. Critical opalescence at the critical point of CO2 near 304 kelvin and 74 bar arises from large-scale density fluctuations on the scale of optical wavelengths. The corresponding states principle collapses gas-liquid coexistence curves for diverse fluids onto a single master curve when scaled by critical temperature and density.

The photon carries momentum h over lambda despite being massless, so light striking a surface exerts radiation pressure. A perfectly absorbing surface feels a pressure equal to the intensity divided by the speed of light, and a perfectly reflecting surface feels twice that. The effect, tiny for ordinary light, is exploited by solar sails and shapes the tails of comets.

The equivalence principle states that the inertial forces felt in an accelerating frame are locally indistinguishable from a gravitational field. An observer in a sealed accelerating rocket cannot tell, by any local experiment, whether the floor pushes up because the rocket accelerates or because a planet pulls down, a thought experiment that guided Einstein toward general relativity.

Fluid flow in the Eulerian description obeys the Navier-Stokes equation rho (du/dt + (u . grad) u) = -grad p + mu Laplacian u + f, where the nonlinear advection term carries the seed of turbulence. The Reynolds number Re = rho u L / mu compares inertial to viscous forces and predicts the onset of turbulence around Re ~ 2000 in pipe flow.

Outgassing limits the lowest pressure attainable in a vacuum system, as gas slowly desorbs from chamber walls long after pumping begins. Water vapour is the dominant contaminant, and baking the chamber at elevated temperature drives off the adsorbed layers, allowing the system to reach the ultrahigh vacuum regime below ten to the minus seven pascals.

Beam emittance epsilon represents the area in transverse phase space occupied by the particle distribution and is conserved under conservative dynamics by Liouville's theorem. Normalised emittance epsilon_n = beta gamma epsilon remains invariant under acceleration. Modern light sources push horizontal emittance below 100 picometre radians by lattice optimisation, while linear colliders aim for vertical emittance of order 10 nanometre radians achieved by damping rings before collision.

A spin echo refocuses the dephasing caused by static field inhomogeneity. A ninety-degree pulse tips the magnetisation into the transverse plane; after a delay tau a one-hundred-eighty-degree pulse reverses the accumulated phases, so that at time 2 tau the spins rephase and produce an echo. The echo amplitude decays with the true T_2 rather than the faster T_2-star set by inhomogeneous broadening.

Rolling friction is far smaller than sliding friction because it arises chiefly from the hysteresis of elastic deformation rather than from interfacial shear. As a wheel rolls, the leading edge of the contact patch compresses and the trailing edge recovers, and the imperfect recovery dissipates energy. The resulting resistance scales with load and inversely with wheel radius, favouring large stiff wheels.

Radiative transfer through an absorbing and emitting medium is described by the equation of transfer, dI / ds = -kappa I + kappa B(T), balancing extinction against thermal emission. In the optically thick limit the radiation field approaches the local Planck function and the transfer reduces to a diffusion process, while in the optically thin limit the emergent intensity is simply the integral of the source emission along the line of sight.

Radiative cooling to the cold sky can drive a surface below ambient air temperature when the surface emits strongly in the eight-to-thirteen micrometre atmospheric transparency window. A material engineered to be highly emissive in this window while reflecting sunlight can cool several degrees below ambient even under direct sun, a passive process exploited in daytime radiative cooling coatings.

Kolmogorov's 1941 theory of homogeneous isotropic turbulence predicts an inertial range energy spectrum E(k) proportional to epsilon^{2/3} k^{-5/3}, where epsilon is the energy dissipation rate per unit mass. The result follows from dimensional analysis assuming statistical scale invariance in the cascade from injection scale to viscous dissipation scale eta = (nu^3/epsilon)^{1/4}. Experimental data span six decades of k consistent with the prediction.

Stokes flow at low Reynolds number obeys linearised Navier-Stokes equations with the inertial term dropped. The drag on a sphere of radius a moving at velocity U through fluid of viscosity mu is F = 6 pi mu a U. Microscopic swimmers operating in this regime, such as bacteria and sperm cells, must use non-reciprocal stroke patterns to achieve net displacement, by Purcell's scallop theorem.

The Madden-Julian Oscillation is the dominant mode of intraseasonal variability in the tropical atmosphere, propagating eastward at about 5 metres per second with a 30 to 60 day period. Convectively active and suppressed phases alternate, organising deep cumulus over the warm pool and modulating monsoons, tropical cyclones, and El Nino onset. Coupling between convection, planetary boundary layer moisture, and large-scale circulation underlies its persistence.

Beats arise when two tones of slightly different frequency superpose, producing a slow amplitude modulation at the difference frequency. The ear hears a single pitch waxing and waning, and the beat rate goes to zero as the two frequencies are brought into unison. Musicians exploit this by tuning an instrument until the beats against a reference tone disappear.

Hydrostatic pressure in a fluid at rest increases linearly with depth as p equals p_0 plus rho g h, independent of the shape of the container. This is the hydrostatic paradox: the pressure at the base depends only on the depth of fluid, so a narrow tall column and a wide shallow basin of the same fluid height exert the same pressure on their bottoms.

Anisotropic conductors carry heat at different rates along different crystallographic directions, so the thermal conductivity becomes a tensor and the heat flux need not be parallel to the temperature gradient. Layered materials such as graphite and pyrolytic boron nitride conduct heat readily within the planes but poorly across them, a property exploited in thermal management to channel heat preferentially.

Group velocity dispersion broadens an optical pulse in a fibre because different spectral components travel at different group velocities. The parameter beta_2, the second derivative of the propagation constant with respect to frequency, sets the rate, and a pulse of bandwidth Delta omega spreads in time by beta_2 L Delta omega over a length L. Telecommunications links compensate this with fibre segments of opposite dispersion sign.

An optical microscope achieves high magnification with a compound arrangement: the objective forms a real magnified intermediate image, which the eyepiece then views as a virtual image at a comfortable distance. The total magnification is the product of the objective and eyepiece magnifications, and the useful upper limit is reached when further magnification reveals only the diffraction-blurred detail.

Accretion onto a compact object releases gravitational binding energy at efficiency epsilon = G M/(R c^2), reaching 10 percent for a neutron star and up to 40 percent for a maximally rotating black hole. The Eddington luminosity L_Edd = 4 pi G M m_p c/sigma_T sets the maximum sustained luminosity at which radiation pressure on accreting electrons balances gravitational attraction. For a solar mass object L_Edd is 1.3 x 10^31 watts.

Steady-state conduction through a plane wall gives a heat flow proportional to the temperature difference and inversely proportional to the wall thickness. Composite walls add their thermal resistances in series, in exact analogy with electrical resistors, so the resistance of an insulating layer adds to that of the structural layer to set the overall heat loss of a building element.

Pattern formation in reaction-diffusion systems was predicted by Turing in 1952. When a homogeneous steady state of two interacting species becomes unstable to spatially modulated perturbations because the inhibitor diffuses faster than the activator, regular spatial patterns of stripes, spots, or labyrinths emerge. The Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction provides a chemical realisation, and similar mechanisms are implicated in animal coat markings and developmental morphogenesis.

Atmospheric drag on a low satellite removes orbital energy, and counterintuitively the satellite speeds up as it descends, because the loss of potential energy outpaces the loss of kinetic energy. The orbit slowly circularises and shrinks until the craft re-enters and burns up. This drag paradox is a direct consequence of the vis-viva relation between speed and orbital radius.

The capillary length, the square root of surface tension over the product of density and gravity, marks the scale below which surface tension dominates over gravity. For water it is a few millimetres, which is why puddles thinner than this bead up while larger bodies of water spread flat under their own weight.

A vibrated layer of grains can support standing-wave patterns of stripes, squares, and hexagons on its surface, much like a driven fluid, but with patterns that oscillate at half the driving frequency. At higher acceleration the layer organises into localised oscillating heaps called oscillons, persistent structures with no counterpart in ordinary fluids.

Elastic waves in a solid separate into longitudinal and transverse modes travelling at different speeds, c_L = sqrt((lambda + 2 mu)/rho) and c_T = sqrt(mu/rho). Because the longitudinal wave is faster, it arrives first, the basis of the primary and secondary wave nomenclature in seismology. At a free surface the two couple into a Rayleigh wave that decays exponentially with depth.

Stick-slip motion occurs when static friction exceeds kinetic friction and a driven object alternately sticks and lurches forward. Elastic energy builds in the driving spring until the static threshold is overcome, then the object slips, the spring relaxes, and the cycle repeats. The phenomenon produces the sound of a bowed violin string, the squeal of brakes, and seismic slip on geological faults.

The human voice generates sound when air forced through the larynx sets the vocal folds into self-sustained oscillation, producing a buzzing source rich in harmonics. The vocal tract then acts as a variable resonator whose formant frequencies shape the spectrum, and the positions of the first two formants distinguish the vowels. Articulation is the act of retuning these acoustic resonances.

Euler buckling of a slender column under axial compression occurs at the critical load P_cr = pi^2 E I / (K L)^2, where I is the second moment of area and K depends on the end conditions. Below this load the straight configuration is stable; above it the column suddenly bows sideways. The instability is a bifurcation, with the buckled shape a half sine wave for pinned ends.

Electron capture is a mode of decay in which an inner atomic electron is absorbed by the nucleus, converting a proton into a neutron and emitting a neutrino. It competes with positron emission whenever the latter is energetically allowed, and dominates when the decay energy is too small to create a positron, leaving a characteristic X-ray as the atomic shell refills.

Bose-Einstein condensation occurs when bosons accumulate macroscopically in the ground state below a critical temperature T_c. For a uniform gas, T_c is set by the condition that the thermal de Broglie wavelength becomes comparable to the interparticle spacing, n lambda_T^3 = zeta(3/2). The condensate fraction grows continuously from zero at T_c.

Johnson-Nyquist noise is the unavoidable voltage fluctuation across a resistor in thermal equilibrium, with mean-square voltage 4 k_B T R per unit bandwidth. The noise originates in the thermal agitation of the charge carriers and sets a fundamental floor on the sensitivity of any electrical measurement. Cooling the resistor or narrowing the bandwidth are the only ways to reduce it.

The stability of a floating body depends on the position of its metacentre, the point where the line of action of the buoyant force crosses the symmetry axis when the body heels. If the metacentre lies above the centre of gravity, a small tilt produces a restoring torque and the body is stable; if below, the torque amplifies the tilt and the body capsizes.

In high-energy particle collisions the relativistic invariant mass of the colliding system, computed from the total energy and momentum four-vector, sets the energy available to create new particles. A fixed-target experiment wastes much of the beam energy on the recoil of the centre of mass, which is why colliding two beams head-on, with zero net momentum, places far more energy at the disposal of particle production.

The fluctuation-dissipation theorem links the random thermal fluctuations of a system to its dissipative response. The Einstein relation, which equates the diffusion coefficient to the mobility times the thermal energy, is the simplest instance: the same molecular collisions that randomly kick a particle also provide the friction that resists its driven motion.

The Karman vortex street shed behind a cylinder in a flow produces a tone at the shedding frequency, given by the Strouhal number times the flow speed divided by the cylinder diameter. This aeolian tone is the singing of telegraph wires in the wind, and when the shedding frequency coincides with a structural resonance the resulting vortex-induced vibration can grow dangerously large.

A ballistic missile follows a near-elliptical trajectory whose apogee lies far above the atmosphere, the powered ascent setting the speed and flight-path angle at burnout. For a given range there exist a low lofted path and a high depressed path, and the minimum-energy trajectory between them resembles a Hohmann-like arc bounded by the spherical Earth.

Plasma sheaths form at the boundary between a quasi-neutral plasma and a material wall, with the wall potential falling below the plasma potential to balance electron and ion fluxes. The Bohm criterion requires ions to enter the sheath at the ion sound speed c_s = sqrt(k_B T_e/m_i). The sheath thickness is several Debye lengths, and the wall potential is roughly minus 3 k_B T_e for hydrogen plasma in floating conditions.

Friction at the atomic scale, studied with the friction force microscope, can exhibit stick-slip on the lattice periodicity, with the tip jumping from one potential well to the next. Under certain conditions of low load and incommensurate contact, the lattice forces cancel and the friction nearly vanishes, a state called structural superlubricity that has been observed between graphite flakes.

Magnetism in transition metal oxides emerges from exchange interactions between localised spins. Superexchange through bridging oxygen anions follows the Goodenough-Kanamori rules: 180-degree cation-anion-cation bonds give strong antiferromagnetic coupling between half-filled orbitals, while 90-degree bonds tend toward ferromagnetic alignment. The resulting magnetic structures range from antiferromagnetic Neel order in NiO to complex helical arrangements in lanthanide manganites.

Pitch perception in the ear is mediated by the basilar membrane, which is mechanically tuned so that high frequencies excite the stiff base and low frequencies the floppy apex. A pure tone produces a localised travelling-wave envelope at a place that depends logarithmically on frequency, providing the place code that underlies the perception of musical pitch.

Polarisation of light is described by the electric field vector orientation. Linearly polarised light has E along a fixed direction; circular polarisation arises from two orthogonal components with a quarter-wave phase difference. A linear polariser transmits intensity according to Malus' law I = I_0 cos^2 theta, where theta is the angle between the polariser axis and the incident polarisation direction.

Shor's algorithm factors an N-bit integer in time polynomial in N, exponentially faster than the best classical algorithms. The quantum subroutine finds the period of f(x) = a^x mod N through the quantum Fourier transform, and a classical post-processing step extracts non-trivial factors. Implementation requires roughly 2N + 3 logical qubits and on the order of N^3 gates, motivating intense effort toward fault-tolerant architectures.

The parallel axis theorem states that the moment of inertia about any axis equals the moment about a parallel axis through the centre of mass plus M d^2, where d is the separation. Combined with the perpendicular axis theorem for planar bodies, I_z = I_x + I_y, these results let one assemble the inertia of a composite body from tabulated values for simple shapes such as rods, discs, and spheres.

A rolling-without-slipping constraint links the translational and rotational coordinates of a wheel through v = R omega and a = R alpha, removing one degree of freedom. A solid cylinder released on an incline accelerates at (2/3) g sin theta because a third of the gravitational work goes into rotational kinetic energy. A hoop, with all its mass at the rim, accelerates at only (1/2) g sin theta and so finishes last in a race.

A torque-free symmetric body executes free precession: in the body frame the angular velocity vector traces a cone about the symmetry axis at the body rate (I_3 - I_1) omega_3 / I_1, while in the inertial frame both omega and the symmetry axis sweep cones about the fixed angular momentum. The Earth's free wobble, the Chandler wobble, is the geophysical realisation with a period near 433 days.

The time-dependent Schrodinger equation i hbar d psi /dt = H psi governs the evolution of a quantum state. For a time-independent Hamiltonian H, stationary states satisfy H psi_n = E_n psi_n, and a general superposition evolves as psi(t) = sum c_n psi_n exp(-i E_n t / hbar). All experimental predictions follow from inner products of states and matrix elements of operators.

The Debye length lambda_D = sqrt(epsilon_0 k_B T_e/(n_e e^2)) sets the screening distance of an electric charge in a plasma, beyond which collective electron motion neutralises the field. A plasma requires the system size to greatly exceed lambda_D and the number of particles in a Debye sphere to be large. The plasma frequency omega_p = sqrt(n_e e^2/(epsilon_0 m_e)) sets the natural oscillation rate of the electron fluid.

The Meissner effect is the expulsion of magnetic flux from the interior of a superconductor as it is cooled below its transition temperature. A superconductor is not merely a perfect conductor but a perfect diamagnet, generating surface currents that cancel the interior field, and the resulting levitation of a magnet above a cooled sample is a direct visual signature of the superconducting state.

Bacterial flagellar motors rotate at hundreds of revolutions per second, powered by the proton motive force across the inner membrane. Each motor contains stator units that deliver torque through electrostatic interactions with the rotor, with stoichiometry adjusted dynamically to the load. The torque-speed curve plateaus at low speed near 1400 piconewton-nanometres and falls sharply above the knee speed of roughly 200 hertz where viscous drag dominates.
